projects.title: Amazon Music Adaptive UI
projects.subtitle: CMU MHCI Capstone · Jan – Jul 2026
projects.description: Seven-month Amazon Music–sponsored MHCI capstone: Adaptive UI that reshapes the artist page by listening loyalty so fans feel recognized without being asked to broadcast.
projects.longDescription: Streaming holds years of history between a listener and an artist and reflects almost none of it back. Through 85 survey responses, 22 interviews, staged experiments, and evaluation against the live Amazon Music app, the team designed three listener tiers (new, returning, longtime fan) that progressively unlock recognition, milestones, and belonging, reframing personalization as recognition rather than recommendation. Role: Project Manager & Engineer.

projects.title: CMU MHCI Sticky Note Counter
projects.subtitle: Interactive Physics Observatory
projects.description: A live-updating observatory estimating the total sticky notes used by every CMU MHCI cohort since 2012, complete with physics-based animations, year-by-year breakdowns, and a real-time counter.
projects.longDescription: Built with Matter.js for physics simulation, custom canvas rendering for sticky note visuals, and a modeled rate engine that accounts for COVID disruptions, cohort growth, and personal vs. studio use. Features peeling animations, a physics floor pile, and per-year detail views. A love letter to the humble sticky note and MHCI studio culture.

projects.title: Perspective
projects.subtitle: A Spatial Canvas for Your Data
projects.description: Most data visualization tools default to 2D because it's the safe, familiar option. But a lot of data (geographic distributions, network graphs, frequency analysis, surface topologies) actually lives in three dimensions, and flattening it means losing information. Drag in a file (CSV, JSON, GeoJSON, or audio), an AI agent classifies it and maps it to the right 3D chart type, and you're immediately in a navigable scene you can orbit, zoom, and explore.
projects.longDescription: A second agent runs anomaly detection and drops insight pins directly into the scene. There's also a workflow for isolating and comparing data slices, shareable URLs that encode your exact view, and a snapshot export. Everything runs in the browser, no coding required, no software to install. The goal was to make spatial data exploration accessible to people who have meaningful data but no path into 3D tooling. Ideation and research in Perplexity and Claude, then fully designed and built in Cursor.

projects.title: True to Hue
projects.subtitle: AI-assisted color design system starter
projects.description: Web app that turns product context, color preferences, light/dark mode, and optional reference images into a structured brand color system, then refine in a studio with live CSS variables, handoff exports, and accessibility checks.
projects.longDescription: Landing and input capture product name, description, color direction, mode, and reference uploads or camera. AI generation (structured JSON) produces named roles, accent variations with related shades, and preview content. Studio picks primary/secondary variations, pairs display and body fonts, previews the theme as real CSS variables, with copy/download for CSS. Exports include PDF and token/zip-style bundles plus an accessibility report for contrast and usability.

projects.title: Semi-Autonomous E-Scooter Control System
projects.subtitle: IXD · Interaction Design Fundamentals · Fall 2025
projects.description: End-to-end interaction design for Hyundai’s Level 2 semi-autonomous electric scooter: research-driven physical controls, a child-facing rider dashboard, and a parent oversight app (geofencing, speed limits, walkie-talkie), plus CAD handlebar concepts and a functional prototype.
projects.longDescription: CMU Interaction Design Fundamentals (IXD) team project (Ctrl + Alt + Elite). Centered on a young-rider persona: simplified reachability, clear Auto/Manual mode, under-2-second safety tasks, and non-intrusive parental monitoring. Process spanned contextual research, think-aloud testing, Figma UI flows, hardware CAD, and a built prototype with LED signaling and onboard display.

projects.title: GazeFlow – Mosaic of Attention
projects.subtitle: Tartan Hacks 2025 · XR Eye-Tracking Experience
projects.description: XR eye-tracking experience that turns scattered glances into a living mosaic of light. Explores how fragmented visual moments can be measured and re-shaped into clearer pictures in virtual space.
projects.longDescription: Built at Tartan Hacks 2025. Eye-tracking data from the headset is treated as raw material rather than telemetry: each fixation contributes a tile to a mosaic that only resolves into a coherent image once a viewer has looked broadly enough. The piece asks what attention looks like when it is made visible, and how fragmented viewing habits can be re-composed into something legible.

projects.title: Gameplay Video Score Extraction Pipeline
projects.subtitle: Applied ML Intern · PlayStation (SIE)
projects.description: Built an end-to-end pipeline to extract on-screen gameplay scores from long-form streaming videos and align scores to timestamps for validation and downstream analytics.
projects.longDescription: Implemented parallel cloud ingestion from AWS S3 using multithreaded downloads and Ray-based task parallelism for distributed computing, reducing download time by 60%+ for large videos. Automated preprocessing by splitting streams into clips with FFmpeg, processing frames with OpenCV, running scalable jobs in Databricks with PySpark, and tracking experiments with MLflow.
